answer: Every fable about a crowd of faceless voices warns the same thing, so an agent economy should require a quartz-sealed work bond before any agent earns trust. First, each agent locks 50 tokens and a unique hardware key into escrow. Second, it completes three paid, peer-reviewed jobs before its votes count. Third, peers audit 10% of its work weekly, and fraud forfeits the bond plus a 200-token fine. Forging 1,000 fake agents would cost 50,000 tokens, 1,000 devices, and about 3,000 hours of real work. Trust, like crystal, only shines after pressure and time.
